newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech shares fall, seen 10 pct down by Christmas.
newsitem.headline: Czech shares fall, seen 10 pct down by Christmas.

text.p: Czech shares continued to decline on Monday with the RPIX index of continuously traded shares hitting an all time low of 1,010 and the broader PX50 moving another 3.5 points below the 500 threshold to 494.9.
Dealers said the decline was likely to continue all the way to Christmas and repeated calls for better regulation of the capital markets to attract investors back into Czech equities.

"The thing that matters is investors don't see protection of investments as being good enough. This is a very hard (perception) to change in the short term," Dan Gladis of Atlantik Financni Trhy said.
Asked where he saw the PX50 at Christmas, he said:
"Ten percent lower by the end of the year with the whole market moving together."
The major issues again applied the bulk of the downward pressure on the index with Komercni Banka the hardest hit.

Komercni lost 50 crowns to 2,030. The PX50's most heavily capitalised share, SPT Telecom fell 25 crowns to 2,835, power utility CEZ, the second most heavily weighted issue, lost five crowns to 950 and Ceska Sporitelna fell three crowns to 323.
In the broader market, insurer Ceska Pojistovna, which on Monday posted nine month gross profits of 85.2 million crowns, fell 41 crowns to 3,450.
